title: Say why a new word matters
statement: Introduce new words through the lesson's purpose and the whole text they serve, not in isolation, and say when a word carries a theme beyond one character or lesson.
detail: Feedback on a Grade 9 prototype's opening word web asked it to stress that the word matters not only for this lesson but as a theme across the whole text, and the review made rewriting a line that tied the words to one character and one lesson a priority item. Its note calls the pattern vocabulary attached to the lesson's purpose rather than defined in isolation, a move seen in two units, which it says makes it worth stating as a rule.

evidence.quote: can we stress the reason we’re starting with this word is not just for this lesson, but it’s a crucial theme across the course of the text?
Rewrite "Today, all of them belong to Iago" so the words are anchored to the whole play rather than to one character and one lesson.
